T2 absolute headroom: NP3-233 outage capacity is ON DISK and IN the target. 107,377 of 119,039 panel hours carry the outage ERCOT had posted before the hour (2014-05 onward; the 11,662 earlier hours get a NULL headroom label, not a False). It averages 13.6 GW and peaked at 35.1 GW, so headroom is 13.6 GW lower than the version every earlier report modelled. The pre-registered 3/5/8 GW thresholds still fire 0/3/9 times in 107,377 hours -- EIA nameplate gas+coal+nuclear sits 10-15 GW above deliverable capacity -- so the reported absolute target is t2_headroom_15gw by the stated rule (smallest fixed threshold with base rate >= 0.3% and >= 25 positives in every era).

phase3_notes.staleness_caveat: Every ERCOT component behind this table and the settled wrapper ratio -- fc_load, fc_wind, fc_solar, fc_outage -- is sampled at 2 vintages/day (the archiver's current per_day setting), so the vintage available at the 10:00 CT decision cut has a median age of roughly 5 h for load/wind/solar and roughly 12 h for outage, not ERCOT's freshest posted vintage. slack_iso (and every *_fc_mw / slack_fc_mw / net_load_fc_mw quantity built on it) is therefore a STALE reconstruction of what ERCOT had published, not the freshest one -- the wrapper ratio compares the model against a deliberately hobbled version of ERCOT's own information, understating how good ERCOT's own forecast actually is at decision time. A fresh-vintage re-test (sampling near every product's 09:00-10:00 CT nearest vintage, >=4/day) is pending. See RESULTS.md S12.
phase3_notes.arms_retraction: RETRACTED (2026-08-30): the "ERCOT-free" independence claim. ix_slack_x_heat, ix_slack_x_solar_ramp, ix_slack_x_disagree, ix_slack_z, and ix_solar_day_range_mw are derived from slack_fc, fc_solar, and load-model disagreement -- all ERCOT-sourced quantities -- yet arms_free_columns.csv marks all five columns in_free_arm=1 (free-eligible). The free arm therefore reads ERCOT forecast products indirectly through these five interaction columns and is NOT independent of ERCOT's own products as claimed. The RTC free_hgb 0.608 BSS cell (verdict.best_by_era.rtc, and verdict.late_winners/free_winners_sig/free_winners_point) stands only as a residual-family result -- an arm that still leans on ERCOT-derived features under a "free" label -- not as evidence that a model with no ERCOT inputs beats slack_iso in the RTC era. A contamination-regression test (lineage tags on every derived column, failing on any descendant of fc_*/slack) is pending; until it lands, treat every free_* cell as resid_*-equivalent. See RESULTS.md S14.

verdicts.text: **pre_ecrs -- ceiling.** The stack LOSES to the naive rule by 0.011 BSS [-0.048, 0.032] on 65,199 hours at a 0.0250 base rate. An oracle on realised net load scores 0.121 against the naive rule's 0.148 -- a margin of -0.027 [-0.085, 0.033], so perfect load foresight is worth less than the model already extracts. Handing the model the target hour's weather (Tier W) moves it by 0.068 [0.042, 0.093]. By base-rate tercile of the test year the margin runs -0.015 (low) / 0.007 (mid) / -0.015 (high). The family whose permutation costs the most PR-AUC is `structure` (0.103). Against the naive rule the model gains 0.0977 Brier per ONSET hour (996 of them) and -0.00111 per quiet hour (62,562), so the onsets carry the margin. Binding constraint: the target itself.

Against the naive rule the model gains 0.1841 Brier per ONSET hour (197 of them) and -0.00162 per quiet hour (4,248), so the onsets carry the margin. Binding constraint: the net-load forecast, not the weather.

claims.text: The hourly-cut hazard model for Deploy (ERS / RUC-for-capacity) at D+1: BSS 0.005 [-0.011, 0.032] vs climatology on only 5 positive days in 1701 rows -- the 95% interval covers zero, not distinguishable from no skill at this label count.

EEA-level operator action has 9 positive days in 4623 rows (2014-01-01 to 2026-08-28) -- too few for any walk-forward split that leaves a test year with positives and a training set to fit on. Not modelled; the base rate is reported and nothing more. Anyone quoting an EEA probability from this repo is quoting noise.

On the untouched 2025-2026 holdout the frozen Meridian two-stage policy dominates NONE of its 6 baselines across the swept ($1k-$1M missed-cost x $0-$30k prep-cost x {1.00, 0.25, 0.05} recovery-loss) region. Against `persistence` -- the hardest baseline to beat -- it wins 90% of the region and loses only where missed_cost <= $30,000 and prep_cost >= $3,000 and recovery_loss <= 0.25. Against `never_prepare`, `climatology_th`, `ercot_public` and `watch_following` it needs a missed tight day worth roughly $30,000-$300,000+ (baseline-dependent, at zero prep cost) before it is cheaper than doing less; below that, preparing less is cheaper and no amount of forecast skill changes it.
